decision: Team-lead decision 2026-10-03 (option '표시 전용'): drug-use chips with no adopted MBPI evidence may show reviewed single-compound or single-peptide literature values, labelled as not entering any score. Team-lead decision 2026-10-04: for the 항진균 and 진통 chips, a species with no single-substance row may show extract-level values (extract, fraction, hydrolysate or polysaccharide of the species) read in the full text, labelled '추출물'.
admission: The organism is the species (accepted name or synonym).

A single compound isolated from the species with the structure elucidated, or a single peptide identified in the species and chemically synthesized (or purified with sequence confirmed). No extracts, fractions, hydrolysates, mixtures or recombinant products.
Not a common metabolite under the 3.1 rule (fatty acids, sterols, carotenoids; Wikidata P703 taxa above the fence of 31).
A numeric value with relation '=' and its unit.
The value was read in the full text or in the curated ChEMBL activity record; abstract-only values wait in 'pending'.

Since 2026-10-04, for 항진균 and 진통 only and only when the species has no single-substance row for that chip: an extract, fraction, hydrolysate or polysaccharide of the species with a numeric result read in the full text (MIC/MFC/IC50 for fungi; a measured response at a stated dose with a significance test for pain models). Inhibition-zone diameters are not concentrations and are not shown.

records.name: holotoxin A
records.assay: Trichophyton rubrum 최소 억제 농도(시험법 미기재)
records.evidence: Kitagawa, Sugawara & Yosioka 1976, Chem Pharm Bull 24(2):275-284, 'Antifungal glycosides from the sea cucumber Stichopus japonicus Selenka (2). Structures of holotoxin A and holotoxin B'. Table III (p.281, MIC µg/ml), read 2026-10-04 from the J-STAGE scan. Holotoxin A, the major antifungal glycoside isolated from the species, has its structure elucidated in this paper; holotoxin B is only 'suggested' there, so its column is not used. The paper does not describe the MIC method or a positive control.
